proposals.before: An edict was issued to the dukes and ministers; grand minister over the masses Dai She and grand minister of works Dou Rong deliberated: 'The five emperors Yuan, Cheng, Ai, and Ping with four generations should replace the present personal temples; Emperors Xuan and Yuan should be honored as grandfather and father and may receive sacrifice in person; from Emperor Cheng downward the officials should perform the rites; separately establish a temple to the imperial father for Lord Nandun.
proposals.after: An edict was issued to the dukes and ministers; grand minister over the masses Dai She and grand minister of works Dou Rong deliberated: 'The five emperors Xuan, Yuan, Cheng, Ai, and Ping, in four generations, should replace the present personal temples; Emperors Xuan and Yuan should be honored as grandfather and father and may receive sacrifice in person; from Emperor Cheng downward the officials should perform the rites; separately establish a temple to the imperial father for Lord Nandun.
proposals.reason: Literal omits Emperor Xuan from the Chinese list 宣、元、成、哀、平五帝, naming only four emperors and starting with Yuan.

proposals.before: Zhang Chun argued that the sage-kings built the Bright Hall and the ritual enclosure to magnify li and yi and to instruct a people already prosperous.
proposals.after: Zhang Chun argued that the sage-kings built the ritual enclosure (biyong) to magnify li and yi and to instruct a people already prosperous.
proposals.reason: Chinese mentions only 辟雍; idiomatic invents a Bright Hall (明堂) not present in this sentence.

proposals.before: Chun held that when the sage kings established the Bright Hall and ringed ritual hall, it was to exalt ritual and righteousness and to teach those already enriched.
proposals.after: Chun held that when the sage kings established the ringed ritual hall (biyong), it was to exalt ritual and righteousness and to teach those already enriched.
proposals.reason: Chinese has only 辟雍; literal invents Bright Hall beside the ritual hall.

proposals.before: Before he could submit it, the erudite Huan Rong submitted a statement that the Bright Hall and Bright Hall ought to be established; the document was sent down to the three dukes and the grand master of ceremonies, and since Chun's opinion agreed with Rong's, the emperor approved.
proposals.after: Before he could submit it, the erudite Huan Rong submitted a statement that the biyong and Bright Hall ought to be established; the document was sent down to the three dukes and the grand master of ceremonies, and since Chun's opinion agreed with Rong's, the emperor approved.
proposals.reason: Literal renders both 辟雍 and 明堂 as Bright Hall, collapsing two distinct institutions.

proposals.before: Four generations back, his ancestor Zhang Anshi had served under Emperor Xuan as grand marshal and general of the guard and had been made marquis of Fuping.
proposals.after: His great-great-grandfather Zhang Anshi had served under Emperor Xuan as grand marshal and general of the guard and had been made marquis of Fuping.
proposals.reason: 高祖父 is specifically great-great-grandfather; 'ancestor' and 'Four generations back' obscure the exact kinship term.

proposals.before: In Jianwu 30 he urged feng and shan: "Since antiquity every true recipient of the mandate, at the zenith of good rule, has mounted Tai to announce success.
proposals.after: In the thirtieth year Chun submitted that feng and shan ought to be performed, saying: "Since antiquity, one who received the mandate and became emperor, at the height of a well-ordered age, invariably performed feng and shan to announce success.
proposals.reason: Idiomatic invents reign name Jianwu and replaces 封禪 with mounted Tai; Chinese has only 三十年 and 封禪.

proposals.before: In the seventeenth year, when Dan'er submitted, Zhang Fen came to court to offer birthday congratulations, was received at Xuanping Hall, answered to the point, and Emperor Ming admired his talent and made him marquis attendant on sacrifice.
proposals.after: In the seventeenth year, when Dan'er submitted, Zhang Fen came to court to offer longevity congratulations, was received at Xuanping Hall, answered to the point, and Emperor Ming admired his talent and made him marquis attendant on sacrifice.
proposals.reason: 上壽 means longevity congratulations, not birthday congratulations.

proposals.before: If I can preserve this man's life while myself bearing the punishment, that is what I wish.'
proposals.after: If I can preserve these persons' lives while myself bearing the punishment, that is what I wish.'
proposals.reason: Chinese 此人命 continues the plural thief case; 'this man's life' is a singular mistranslation.

proposals.before: He was made attendant-in-chief and joined the southern tour; on return the case went to the three dukes, but before they reported the emperor called in Ban Gu of the Black Tortoise office to ask how ritual ought to be revised.
proposals.after: He was made palace attendant and joined the southern tour; on return the case went to the three dukes, but before they reported the emperor called in Ban Gu of the Black Tortoise office to ask how ritual ought to be revised.
proposals.reason: 侍中 is palace attendant, as correctly rendered for the same office at s0274; 'attendant-in-chief' invents a different title.

proposals.before: When the emperor died and He succeeded, Cao Bao wrote glosses; the new ruler then prefixed two fascicles as the New Rites.
proposals.after: When the emperor died and Emperor He succeeded, Cao Bao wrote glosses; the emperor then used two chapters of the New Rites for the capping ceremony.
proposals.reason: 以《新禮》二篇冠 means employing two Xin li chapters for the capping (冠) rite, not prefixing fascicles; also 'He' alone is opaque for 和帝.

proposals.before: When the emperor died and Emperor He ascended, Bao then composed commentaries on it; the emperor thereupon prefixed two chapters as the Xin li.
proposals.after: When the emperor died and Emperor He ascended, Bao then composed commentaries on it; the emperor thereupon used two chapters of the Xin li for the capping.
proposals.reason: 冠 here is the capping ceremony, not 'prefixed'; the literal invents a book-prefixing sense absent from the Chinese.

proposals.before: Later he was dismissed for sitting on a false report about disasters.
proposals.after: Later he was dismissed for the offense of inaccurate reporting of disasters.
proposals.reason: 坐…免 means convicted/dismissed for an offense; 坐 does not mean physically sitting on a report.

proposals.before: He therefore went to the imperial academy to pursue studies, served as disciple to the fifth Yuanxian of the capital region, and first mastered the Jing lineage Changes, the Gongyang Spring and Autumn, the Triple Concordance calendar, and the Nine Chapters on mathematical procedures.
proposals.after: He therefore went to the imperial academy to pursue studies, served as disciple to Fifth Yuanxian of the capital region, and first mastered the Jing lineage Changes, the Gongyang Spring and Autumn, the Triple Concordance calendar, and the Nine Chapters on mathematical procedures.
proposals.reason: 第五 is the compound surname Fifth/Diwu; lowercasing fifth wrongly treats it as an ordinal rather than the name.

proposals.before: The clerks replied: 'These for the most part are persons without posterior heirs since the Jianwu era onward, and they could not obtain burial.'
proposals.after: The clerks replied: 'These for the most part are persons without heirs since the Jianwu era onward, and they could not obtain burial.'
proposals.reason: posterior heirs is unnatural English for 絕無後者; heirs alone preserves the sense.

proposals.before: General of the Rear Yuan Wei recommended him for attendant-in-chief, but mourning for his father kept him from accepting.
proposals.after: General of the Rear Yuan Wei recommended him for Palace Attendant, but mourning for his father kept him from accepting.
proposals.reason: 侍中 is Palace Attendant, not attendant-in-chief.

proposals.before: Later General of the Rear Yuan Wei memorialized him as attendant-in-chief, but because of his father's mourning he did not take up the post.
proposals.after: Later General of the Rear Yuan Wei memorialized him as Palace Attendant, but because of his father's mourning he did not take up the post.
proposals.reason: 侍中 is Palace Attendant, not attendant-in-chief.

proposals.after: Ying Shao had a shamefaced look.
proposals.reason: Bare Shao is ambiguous with Yuan Shao in neighboring units; the subject is Ying Shao.

proposals.before: All told he glossed the Changes, Documents, Mao Odes, Ceremonial, Book of Rites, Analects, Filial Piety, Amplified Documents, Zhong hou, and the Qian xiang calendar, and wrote treatises on the seven celestial governors, Lu di and xia, the six arts, the Mao ode stemma, a refutation of Xu Shen's divergent glosses, and a reply to Lin Xiaocun's Zhou li critique—well over a million characters.
proposals.after: All told he glossed the Changes, Documents, Mao Odes, Ceremonial, Book of Rites, Analects, Filial Piety, Amplified Documents, Zhong hou, and the Qian xiang calendar, and wrote treatises on the seven celestial governors, the Lu ritual meaning of di and xia, the six arts, the Mao ode stemma, a refutation of Xu Shen's divergent glosses, and a reply to Lin Xiaocun's Zhou li critique—well over a million characters.
proposals.reason: Idiomatic 'Lu di and xia' omits 禮 and obscures 魯禮禘祫義; literal has 'Lu ritual meaning of di and xia'.

proposals.before: The judgment says: From the time Qin burned the Six Arts, the sage texts were dust and extinction.
proposals.after: The judgment says: From the time Qin burned the Six Classics, the sage texts were dust and extinction.
proposals.reason: Chinese has 六經 (Six Classics); literal wrongly renders Six Arts (六藝).

decisions.reason: s0022 lists 宣、元、成、哀、平五帝; the literal omitted 宣 and named only four emperors, so restoring Xuan is required.
s0050 has only 建辟雍; 明堂 is not in this sentence, so removing the invented Bright Hall is correct.
The same unit mentions only 辟雍; inventing Bright Hall beside the ritual hall is unsupported.

decisions.after: Before he could submit it, the erudite Huan Rong submitted a statement that the ritual enclosure (biyong) and the Bright Hall ought to be established; the document was sent down to the three dukes and the grand master of ceremonies, and since Chun's opinion agreed with Rong's, the emperor approved.
decisions.reason: s0052 has 宜立辟雍、明堂 as two institutions; the original collapsed both as Bright Hall. The proposal correctly splits them, but bare 'biyong' is less natural than the parallel 'ritual enclosure (biyong)' used elsewhere.
高祖父 is four generations back; the idiomatic already states that accurately. Preferring 'great-great-grandfather' is stylistic, not a factual repair.
s0053 has only 三十年 and 封禪; inventing the reign title Jianwu and replacing feng-shan with 'mounted Tai' adds content absent from the Chinese.
上壽 is a longevity toast/congratulations, not a birthday greeting; the idiomatic misread the ritual act.
Context s0107–s0110 treats the arrested thieves in the plural (殺之 / 不為殺); 此人命 continues that plural case, so singular 'this man's life' is wrong.
侍中 is the palace attendant office; 'attendant-in-chief' invents a different title.
帝遂以《新禮》二篇冠 uses 冠 as the capping rite applied with two Xin li chapters, not as prefixing fascicles; clarifying 和帝 as Emperor He is also needed.
The same 冠 is the capping ceremony; 'prefixed two chapters as the Xin li' invents a book-prefixing sense absent from the Chinese.
坐上災害不實免 is the legal idiom 'dismissed for the offense of…'; 坐 does not mean physically sitting on a report.
第五元先 is the compound surname 第五 plus given name 元先; lowercased 'fifth' wrongly reads it as an ordinal.
絕無後者 is already intelligible as 'without posterior heirs'; dropping 'posterior' is stylistic polish, not a meaning error.
表為侍中 names Palace Attendant; 'attendant-in-chief' is the wrong office title.
The literal has the same false title for 侍中; Palace Attendant is the correct rendering.
劭有慚色 refers to Ying Shao (應劭) from s0235; bare 'Shao' is ambiguous beside Yuan Shao (紹) in s0235/s0238.
《魯禮禘祫義》 includes 禮; 'Lu di and xia' drops that and obscures the treatise title.
秦焚《六經》 is Six Classics; rendering Six Arts (六藝) is a different phrase and wrong here.
